About
Children in Year 1 participate in the Club's junior cricket programme, which aims to teach fundamental cricket at this level. The programme is built around a series of different skill modules and games to provide a fun and varied programme each week. Experience has shown us that children of this age do not have the attention span to play full games of cricket and not only enjoy this varied programme more but also learn better fundamental skills to prepare them for games in Year 2. later on in the season players will regularly participate in limited over games against each other to test their new-found skills in action.
All parents are expected to help, when they can, in these weekly sessions and the Club runs a pre-season training module for parents in order to prepare for this. Children get far more out of sport when their parents or caregivers become actively involved plus, with as many adults as possible involved each week, the burden does not fall on just one or two people and everyone gets to enjoy their involvement.
## More information
### Where
All Year 1 cricket will take place on Friday afternoons in front of the Parnell Cricket Clubrooms at Shore Road Reserve (Near the children's playground). 
These after-school sessions are supervised by the Club's qualified cricket coaches. Parent assistance is encouraged.  
Note that the players are not allocated to specific teams in Year 1. 
There are NO mid-week practice sessions for this age group.
Start time is 4.45pm and the sessions generally finish around 6.00pm. The Club operates a BBQ sausage sizzle during the evening and the bar will be open for refreshments. 
### Season dates
Start date: 
 Friday 30th October 2026.
 Last playing date pre-Christmas: 
 Friday 18th December 2026.
 Restart post-Christmas:  
 Friday 5th February 2027. 
Final playing date for the season:  
 Friday 19th March 2027.
Cancellations:
If the weather is such that play is not possible then these sessions will be cancelled. The Club will advise all players via email by 2.45pm if the session is to cancelled.
All cricket equipment for this grade is provided by the Club so there is no need to invest in cricket gear until you are sure of your child's commitment.

###### Years 2, 3 & 4 Cricket 
These softball grades are suitable for boys and girls in School Years 2, 3 & 4.
PLAYING DATES 2026/27:
The Pre-Christmas Season runs from Friday 30th October to Friday 18th December 2026.
The Post-Christmas Season commences Friday 5th January and concludes Friday 19th March 2027.
 POST-CHRISTMAS DRAWS
The post-Christmas draws can be found here: (To be updated in due course).
[https://www.playhq.com/new-zealand-cricket/org/eastern-districts-cricket-association/summer-202425/9114d08e](https://www.playhq.com/new-zealand-cricket/org/eastern-districts-cricket-association/summer-202425/9114d08e)
 ABOUT
Our Year 2, 3 and 4 teams are 8-a-side and play in the Eastern Districts Cricket Association (EDCA) competition, which involves three other local Clubs-Grafton United CC, Auckland University CC and Ellerslie CC. 
For the 2026-27 season, all matches will be played on Friday evenings.
Pre-Christmas, all games will be played at Shore Road Reserve on Fridays from 5.00pm. (Internal games only).
However post-Christmas, some games will also be played at the opposition's home ground (AUCC, Grafton or Ellerslie), depending on the draw. (Also all played on Friday evenings).
Limited-over games start at 5.00 pm on Fridays and are approximately 1.5 to 2 hours in duration. Rules are formatted so that all children get the opportunity to participate equally throughout the game. All three grades play with a Junior size Incrediball (soft ball).
TEAM PRACTICE TIMES
Weekly team practices will generally be held on Tuesday, Wednesday or Thursday evenings from 4.00-5.00 pm or 5.00-6.00 pm, at [Shore Road Reserve or Thomas Bloodworth Park](https://www.parnellcricket.co.nz/ground-maps). Actual practice day and time will be confirmed by your team coach. 
In addition, our Pro-Coaches lead a series of weekly technical skills sessions for our Year’s 3 & 4 players. These sessions are held at the Shore Road outdoor nets.
[Please click here](https://www.parnellcricket.co.nz/s/Pro-Coaching-2023-24.pdf) to see the pro-coaching timetable.
TEAM ALLOCATIONS
The Club Policy is that all players should play in their correct grade. However, it does allow children to play up (or down) a grade depending on friends and abilities, but once a child is in School Year 4 (as at the start of a cricket season) they MUST play in the corresponding Year 4 cricket grade. This will mean that some children may have to repeat Year 4 if they were playing up a grade the season before.
All our teams are selected to provide a mix of abilities and schools as much as possible. Our grade coordinators do their utmost to accommodate team friend requests within these guidelines, usually with highly successful outcomes. However, we can offer no guarantees and appreciate your understanding that not all requests can be met.
PLAYER EQUIPMENT
All cricket equipment is provided in a team gear bag so there is no need to invest in cricket gear until you are sure of your child's commitment. 
Please contact our Year 2, 3 or 4 Grade Coordinator for more information

These grades are suitable for boys and girls in Years 5 - 8.

Our Under 11, 12 & 13 Hardball teams compete in the Saturday morning T20 Smash Grades around greater Auckland with the competitions split regionally with other Clubs close by to minimize travel.

Dispensation must be given by Auckland Cricket to those players who wish to play down a grade.

## Junior boys/mixed grades Winter Academy.
Registrations for the 2026 Winter Academy are now open.
The primary focus is on skills development via a pathway program that will enable our junior and youth cricketers to be the best they can. 
The outcome is to prepare our aspiring cricketers for the various stages of their intermediate and college years and ultimately into senior cricket assisting in developing a lifelong love of cricket within the Parnell Cricket Club.
 Registration 
 Please note that you should register your child in the Grade in which he/she will be playing in the upcoming 2026-27 season
Please click on the appropriate link below:
[Under 10](https://www.playhq.com/new-zealand-cricket/register/6e6664)
[Under 11](https://www.playhq.com/new-zealand-cricket/register/6e6664)
[Under 12](https://www.playhq.com/new-zealand-cricket/register/6e6664)
[Under 13](https://www.playhq.com/new-zealand-cricket/register/6e6664)
[Year 9 & 10](https://www.playhq.com/new-zealand-cricket/register/6e6664)
[Year 11-13](https://www.playhq.com/new-zealand-cricket/register/6e6664) 
### Academy dates:
[Please download the info sheet for dates for each age group](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/650e4c20299a53936d88c704/69dc2748bbaf44b1ced6f11a_Parnell%20Cricket%20Club%20%E2%80%93%20Winter%20Academies%202026.pdf)
### Details of each academy
### Under 10
Designed for players who partook in Grade 4 during the 2025/26 season 
This academy has a focus on understanding the basics of hardball cricket e.g. how to wear equipment appropriately, seam position with a hardball etc
Cost $250. 
### Under 11 & 12
Designed for players who partook in Under 10 and Under 11 respectively during the 2025/26 season. The academy looks at Age and Stage rules set by Auckland Cricket and how to adapt your game to benefit while playing JTS cricket e.g. players have a grace period to begin their innings, how should it be used?
Cost $290 
### Under 13
Designed for players who partook in Under 12 during the 2025/26 season. The academy looks at Colts and College Sport cricket; the change in format, recognising that your physique will change drastically etc.
Cost $290 
### Year 9 & 10
Designed for players currently in year 9 or 10. This academy has been amended this winter to better reflect the successful Future Peaches Academy. The academy will look at how to best perform in Colts & 1st/2nd XI college cricket, but also an introduction to Parnell's senior program and opportunity this provides e.g. training with senior teams during the summer holidays
Cost $290 
In addition, some players from within this academy will be invited to train with the Future Peaches where opportunities arise
Cost $320 
### Year 11 - 13 (Future Peaches)
Designed by Ian West five years ago, this academy was designed to link our eldest youth players to the senior club, with resounding success. The academy looks to benefit participants regardless of their college team selection, with a view to involve them in the Parnell Senior set-up
Cost $320 
### Purpose
To provide the most appropriate environments and program to develop and support our school age cricketers allowing them to achieve the goals of reaching the appropriate age group team right into senior cricket. Allowing them to be “the best they can be”.
In order to identify, nurture and develop our school age cricketers. The club has created a pathway program which identifies these groups into specific age groups then will undertake a skill based winter academy program.
The programme will include seven to eight skill sessions led by Ian West and assisted by our excellent Parnell CC coaching staff. We will also have the ability to run specific skills sessions utilising our key coaches.
The program will culminate with the groups playing pre-season matches prior to the commencement of the new season and the future peaches joining the premier squad in some pre-season trainings and matches.

## Championship Grades / One Day Grades
Parnell Cricket have a number of One day teams available to join. These teams play throughout the season from Labour weekend till the end of March.
 Team Registration & Subscriptions
Team registration and payment of subscriptions should be made by the team captain/manager. Simply click on the button above and then select the REGISTER TEAM tab
One Day team's subscription for the 2025-26 season is $2,940.
All team subscriptions must be paid in full prior to the start of the season.
### Training
Training sessions are decided by the teams’ captain but are usually held at the Shore Road nets on Wednesday evenings, commencing at 6 pm. 
The Shore Road nets are reserved for Parnell CC members at all times. Nets are reserved for junior club members from 4pm-6pm, and senior members from 6pm onwards, from Monday – Friday. This is from a safety point of view. 
### Team Registration & Subscriptions
Registrations for the 2025-26 playing season are now open. Team registration and payment of subscriptions should be made by the team captain/manager. 
The full season’s team subscription is $2,160 (GST Incl.) for T20 grades and $2,940 for One Day teams. All subscriptions must be paid in full prior to the start of the season.
### Uniform
 Players should wear the Parnell Cricket Club polo shirt and white shorts, available from Players Sports. Suitable footwear should be worn (no bare feet!), and all batsmen must wear a cricket helmet when batting.
### Scoring
 Scoring will be done using PlayHQ. Results of all games must be entered in PlayHQ by 5 pm on the Monday after the weekend of play. 
### Contact
Any person who wishes to organise their own One Day Grade team should also contact Mark Hooper, Parnell’s Director of Cricket, on [027 246 3848](tel:+64272463848) or [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#4e232f3c250e3e2f3c202b22222d3c272d252b3a602d21602034) for details.

## About
Children in Year 0/1 - 2 participate in the Club's junior cricket programme, which aims to teach fundamental cricket at this level. The programme is built around a series of different skill modules and games to provide a fun and varied programme each week. Experience has shown us that children of this age do not have the attention span to play full games of cricket and not only enjoy this varied programme more but also learn better fundamental skills to prepare them for games in Year 2. later on in the season players will regularly participate in limited over games against each other to test their new-found skills in action.
All parents are expected to help, when they can, in these weekly sessions and the Club runs a pre-season training module for parents in order to prepare for this. Children get far more out of sport when their parents or caregivers become actively involved plus, with as many adults as possible involved each week, the burden does not fall on just one or two people and everyone gets to enjoy their involvement.
## More information
### Where
All Year 1-4 cricket will take place on Friday afternoons in front of the Parnell Cricket Clubrooms at Shore Road Reserve (Near the children's playground).
These after school sessions are supervised by the Club's qualified cricket coaches. Parent assistance is encouraged.  
Note that the players are not allocated to specific teams in Year 1.
Start time is 4.45pm and the sessions generally finish around 6.00pm. The Club operates a BBQ sausage sizzle during the evening and the bar will be open for refreshments. There are NO mid-week practice sessions for this age group.
### Season dates
Start date:

### Cancellations
If the weather is such that play is not possible then these sessions will be cancelled. The Club will advise all players via email by 3.00pm if the session will be cancelled.
All cricket equipment for this grade is provided by the Club so there is no need to invest in cricket gear until you are sure of your child's commitment.

### Fees & Registrations

Online registrations for our Term 2 Junior and Youth Academies are now open. Please contact [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection) for more information.
## Academies
### Junior Girls' Years 3 & 4 and 5 & 6 Softball Winter Academy 
Our Junior Girls Cricket Winter Softball programme has been designed to build confidence and skills in girls who are playing Junior grade ‘softball’ cricket (U9 & U11).
The programme will include 60min sessions led by our PCC Pro-Coaches and Youth Girl coaches. Focused on skill development across batting, bowling and fielding in small groups (based on ability) rather than age, giving the girls the best opportunity to develop their skills and confidence ahead of the cricket season starting in Term 4.
### Junior Girls' Years 5 & 6 Hardball Winter Academy
Our Junior Girls Winter Hardball programme has been designed to build confidence and skills in girls who will be playing U11 grade hardball cricket in the 26/27 cricket season. The programme will include 60min sessions led by our PCC Pro-Coaches and Youth Girl coaches.
The sessions will be focused on skill development across batting, bowling and fielding in small groups (based on ability) rather than age, giving the girls the best opportunity to develop their skills and confidence ahead of the cricket season starting in Term 4.
### Intermediate Girls' Years 7 & 8 Winter Academy
Our Intermediate Girls Winter Academy has been designed to nurture and develop School Cricket and U13 club players with a focus on skill development across the technical, tactical and mental aspects of cricket.
The programme will include 60min sessions led by our PCC Pro-Coaches and Youth Girl coaches.
The sessions will be focused on skill development across batting, bowling and fielding in small groups (based on ability) rather than age, giving the girls the best opportunity to develop their skills and confidence ahead of the cricket season starting in Term 4.
### Youth Girls' Years 9 & 10 Winter Academy
Our Youth Girls Winter Academy has been designed to nurture and develop School (College Sport) Cricket and U16 club players with a focus on skill development across the technical and tactical aspects of cricket.
The programme will include 90 min sessions led by our PCC Pro-Coaches, Baradene and Epsom Girls' coaches as well as guest coaches including former White Ferns.
These sessions will be fast paced with a mix of whiteboard and practical coaching delivered in a fun and safe environment giving the girls the best opportunity to develop their skills within a setting of girls coached alongside players of the same ability rather than by age group.
### Senior Girls Years 11 - 13 Academy
Our Senior Girls Academy has been designed to challenge and develop girls currently playing College Sport, U16 and Senior club cricket with a focus on skill development across tactical and mental as well as technical aspects of cricket. 
The programme will include 90 min sessions led by our PCC Pro-Coaches, Baradene and Epsom Girls' coaches as well as guest coaches including former White Ferns.
These sessions will be fast paced with a mix of whiteboard and practical coaching delivered in a fun and safe environment giving the girls the best opportunity to develop their skills within a setting of girls coached alongside players of the same ability rather than by age group.

# Polly Inglis earning her first White Ferns contract
July 22, 2024
# 
### 
#### 
### 
#### 
Share this page on:
[](#)[](#)
Congratulations for Polly Inglis earning her first White Ferns contract.
Polly played for PCC 2017/18 to 2018/19 season scoring 250 runs at 27.78 with one century 100 not out.
Full news can be found here:
https://www.1news.co.nz/2024/06/11/polly-inglis-earns-first-white-ferns-contract-offer/
A day after Black Sticks veteran Hugo Inglis won the Nations Cup with the NZ men's hockey team in Poland, the Inglis household has another reason to celebrate.
Sister Polly has been named as the lone newcomer in the White Ferns' contract list.
“We joke about Hugo being the favourite child a lot," laughed Polly.
"I guess it's been an inspiration to try and take the number one spot."
Inglis’ offer comes after she featured in the New Zealand A side that beat England A in a one-day home series in March.
An Otago Sparks mainstay since 2012, the 28-year-old was pivotal for the side in this year’s Hallyburton Johnstone Shield campaign.
She finished as the competition’s second-highest run-scorer with a calm 35 not out in the final against the Wellington Blaze to help the Southerners secure the one day title.
“She certainly got an education on how to field," joked brother Hugo.
"We didn't let her bat or bowl too often, but she was an, an excellent fielder."
Coach Ben Sawyer said planning for the next Women’s Cricket World Cup was a key selection focus.
Sawyer said Inglis’ performances have made her the first pick for back-up wicketkeeper.
“We've definitely had our eye on Polly for a while, in particular as a keeper/bat. I want to stress that - the batting and what she brings is important as well.”
The 28-year-old thanks her hockey background for that. A promising player in that code, she played in the National Hockey League and was also selected for the Development Black Sticks.
“I guess once they see me bat, they might notice a bit of a hockey swing," she said.
"I got the opportunity to go to England and play county cricket over there and learnt chasing the summers was pretty fun. – So, I continued with that.
"I just want to play with as much confidence as possible and enjoy it because playing for your country is a bit of an honour. "
The 2024-25 contracting period begins August 1 and the players have until June 17 to accept their offer.
The White Ferns depart for their tour to England on Thursday.
Contract offers have
WHITE FERNS central contract offers 2024-25: Suzie Bates, Eden Carson, Sophie Devine, Lauren Down, Izzy Gaze, Maddy Green, Brooke Halliday, Polly Inglis, Hayley Jensen, Fran Jonas, Jess Kerr, Melie Kerr, Rosemary Mair, Molly Penfold, Georgia Plimmer, Hannah Rowe, Lea Tahuhu
[By Michelle Prendiville, 1News Sport Reporter](https://www.1news.co.nz/reporter/michelle-prendiville/)

Post from Desley Simpson - Deputy Mayor of Auckland
Want to know what is happening behind the fence at Thomas Bloodworth Park? Well it’s Lots 
1. Bridge - All 3 bridge treads will be demolished and replaced. As well as the installation of new non slip mesh, new handrails and balustrades.
2. Fence - The rotten picket fence will be renewed and painted Karaka green, a mowing strip will also be installed for ease of maintenance and durability
